items.docs: Returns the accounts the authenticated user has been granted access to, with pagination and filtering. Supports `?include=roles` to sideload the user's RBAC roles on each account; when present, each account gains a `relationships.roles` object and the related role resources are returned in the top-level `included` array.

items.docs: Provisions a new user in the Decisiv SRM ecosystem. This endpoint is **not** idempotent: a duplicate email or username — including one belonging to a discarded user — is rejected with `422`, matching the legacy vendor self-registration and admin-create flows. A welcome notification is sent automatically on success — either a password setup email or an SSO welcome email depending on the user's email domain.

params.name: include
params.description: Sideload related resources (e.g. `roles`)

params.name: filter[email]
params.description: Filter by exact email address

params.name: filter[first_name:like]
params.description: Filter by first name (partial, case-insensitive)

params.name: filter[last_name:like]
params.description: Filter by last name (partial, case-insensitive)

params.name: filter[external_reference.business_system]
params.description: Filter by the user's business-system identifier (the same value returned in `external_reference.business_system`).

params.name: filter[roles.id]
params.description: Filter by role ID. Accepts a comma-separated list; users must have ALL listed roles on this account (AND). Example: filter[roles.id]=1,2

params.name: filter[roles.id:includes]
params.description: Filter by role ID. Accepts a comma-separated list; users must have ANY of the listed roles on this account (OR). Example: filter[roles.id:includes]=1,2

params.name: filter[roles.id:excludes]
params.description: Filter by role ID. Accepts a comma-separated list; returns users who do NOT have ANY of the listed roles on this account. Example: filter[roles.id:excludes]=1,2

params.name: filter[job_role]
params.description: Filter by exact `job_role` (e.g. `Branch Manager`). Pass the same value returned in the `job_role` attribute on the response.

params.name: filter[job_role:like]
params.description: Filter by partial `job_role` match (case-insensitive). Example: `Manager` matches users whose `job_role` is `Branch Manager` or `Service Manager`.

params.name: filter[last_login_at:gte]
params.description: Filter to users whose most recent login is on or after the given ISO 8601 timestamp. Example: filter[last_login_at:gte]=2026-01-01T00:00:00Z

params.name: filter[last_login_at:lte]
params.description: Filter to users whose most recent login is on or before the given ISO 8601 timestamp.

params.name: filter[last_login_at:exists]
params.description: Filter users by whether a `last_login_at` timestamp exists. Use `true` to list only users who have logged in at least once, or `false` to list only users who have never logged in.

params.name: sort
params.description: Sort the results. Accepts a comma-separated list of fields; prefix any field with `-` for descending. The first field is the primary sort key; subsequent fields break ties. Allowed fields: `last_login_at`, `roles.name`, `job_role`. Examples: `sort=last_login_at`, `sort=-job_role`, `sort=roles.name,-last_login_at`. Defaults to `last_name asc, first_name asc` when omitted. For `roles.name`, multi-role users are placed by their alphabetically first role (asc) or last role (desc) on this account. Empty/null values for any sortable column are always grouped at the end (NULLS LAST) regardless of direction.

items.docs: List all users assigned to an account. Supports `?include=roles` to sideload role assignments.

info.name: Add a user to an account

items.docs: Assigns an existing ecosystem user to an account with one or more roles. If the user was previously removed, their account access is reactivated.
Retrieve a single user within an account context.

info.name: Update an account user's communication preferences

items.docs: Updates the per-account visibility flags for a user already associated with the account. Any subset of `communication_preferences` keys may be supplied; omitted keys are left unchanged. Returns 404 if the user has no role assignments in this account.

info.name: Remove a user from an account

items.docs: Deactivates a user's access to an account. Removes all role assignments, group memberships, user permissions, and recipient records. Cannot remove yourself.

info.name: Add roles to an account user

items.docs: Assign one or more additional roles to a user within an account.

info.name: Remove a role from an account user

params.name: id
params.description: The role ID to remove

items.docs: Remove a single role from a user within an account. Cannot remove the last role (use DELETE /users/{id} instead) or modify your own roles.

params.name: filter[name]

params.name: filter[name:like]
params.description: List `roles` that partially match the `name` attribute (case-insensitive). Accepts a comma-separated list of values to match any of them (OR). Wildcard characters in the value are matched as literal characters, not wildcards.
